answer: Each PoA identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where each result determines the next, before producing a compact Wesolowski proof. GPUs can accelerate separate chains, but cannot divide one chain into independent steps; every added clone therefore requires its own sequential run and elapsed time. Quartz, falcon, and prism labels do not bypass this physical bottleneck, which makes Sybil identities costly to create quickly.
